title: Basutoland
capsule: Basutoland was a British Crown Colony established in 1884 when the British government assumed direct control from the Cape Colony, which had administered it since 1871 following the Gun War. The territory had been consolidated by Moshoeshoe I (r. 1822–1870), the founder of the Basotho nation, who sought British protection to resist Boer encroachment from the Orange Free State. Basutoland remained a separate protectorate outside the Union of South Africa (which the three High Commission Territories—Basutoland, Bechuanaland, and Swaziland—deliberately avoided), and became the independent Kingdom of Lesotho on 4 October 1966.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Basutoland's boundaries were formally delimited and are well-documented in colonial records; they correspond closely to modern Lesotho.
